name: XIRR
description: XIRR returns the annualized internal rate of return for cash flows occurring at irregular intervals.
tldr: Calculates the internal rate of return for a schedule of cash flows that is not necessarily periodic.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Series of cash flows corresponding to the dates.

parameters.name: dates
parameters.description: Series of dates corresponding to the cash flows.

basicExample.explanation: A2:A5 contains dates, and B2:B5 contains the corresponding cash flows.

advancedExamples.title: Add a guess
advancedExamples.description: Provide a guess to help the solver converge
advancedExamples.explanation: A 20% guess can help when the default guess fails.

howItWorks: XIRR solves for the rate that makes the net present value of the irregular cash flows equal to zero. It uses an annualized rate based on the 365-day year.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Dates must be valid and in chronological order.
Requires at least one positive and one negative cash flow.

commonErrors.cause: The solver cannot converge or the cash flows have the same sign.
commonErrors.fix: Add a guess or check that cash flows have both signs.

commonErrors.cause: Dates are not valid or do not align with values.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure dates are valid Excel dates and match the values array.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: XIRR works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between IRR and XIRR?
faq.answer: IRR assumes equal-period cash flows. XIRR uses actual dates for irregular intervals.

faq.question: Can XIRR handle monthly contributions?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as the dates are provided, the intervals can be any length.
